stories.title: CISA Adds 5 Actively Exploited Artifactory, ScreenConnect, and RouterOS Flaws to KEV
stories.abstract: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to include five security flaws affecting JFrog Artifactory, ConnectWise ScreenConnect, and MikroTik RouterOS. These vulnerabilities are currently being leveraged by threat actors in active attacks, necessitating immediate attention from system administrators.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are actively exploited in the wild, posing a high risk of unauthorized access or privilege escalation within critical infrastructure environments.
stories.action: Update JFrog Artifactory, ConnectWise ScreenConnect, and MikroTik RouterOS to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: GitLab CVSS 10 File-Read Flaw Draws In-the-Wild Probes After Disclosure
stories.abstract: GitLab has patched a critical path traversal vulnerability, CVE-2026-85706, affecting versions 19.1, 19.2, and 19.3. The flaw enables unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files from the server and is currently being actively exploited in the wild.
stories.why: This critical vulnerability allows unauthorized access to sensitive server files and is already under active exploitation, posing an immediate risk to infrastructure.
stories.action: Update GitLab instances to versions 19.1.8, 19.2.6, or 19.3.2 immediately.

stories.title: Cisco FMC Flaws Exploited to Steal Credentials and Deploy Qilin Ransomware
stories.abstract: Cisco, Citrix, and Fortinet have patched critical vulnerabilities now confirmed to be under active exploitation by ransomware groups and state-sponsored actors. These flaws, including an authentication bypass in Cisco FMC, allow remote attackers to gain unauthorized access and deploy malicious payloads.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are being actively weaponized in the wild to facilitate ransomware deployment and credential theft, posing a high risk to enterprise infrastructure.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches for Cisco FMC, ASA, FTD, Citrix, and Fortinet products immediately.

stories.title: Check Point Discloses Two 9.8-Rated VPN Certificate Flaws Enabling Unauthenticated RCE
stories.abstract: The Dutch NCSC has issued an urgent warning regarding two critical vulnerabilities in Check Point VPN products. These flaws, which allow for unauthenticated remote code execution, are reportedly facing imminent exploitation attempts, necessitating immediate attention from administrators managing affected security gateways.
stories.why: Unauthenticated remote code execution on perimeter security appliances represents a high-risk entry point for threat actors to gain full network access.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches provided by Check Point immediately.

stories.title: ConnectWise security advisory (AV26-903) – Update 1
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities are actively exploited in ConnectWise ScreenConnect and MikroTik RouterOS. CISA has added several of these flaws, including CVE-2026-84869, CVE-2026-67277, and CVE-2026-86060, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, necessitating immediate patching for affected infrastructure.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities allow unauthorized access or control, and their active exploitation in the wild poses an immediate risk to enterprise networks.
stories.action: Update ScreenConnect to 26.6.5 and patch MikroTik RouterOS to the latest supported versions immediately.

stories.title: China-Linked UNC3569 Exploited Sogou Input Method Flaw to Deploy GRAYRABBIT Backdoor
stories.abstract: A China-aligned threat actor is exploiting a critical vulnerability in the Tencent Sogou Input Method for Windows. By leveraging a malicious link, attackers can achieve arbitrary code execution, allowing them to install the GrayRabbit backdoor and gain full control over the victim's system.
stories.why: This represents a supply chain-style compromise of a widely used utility, providing attackers with high-privilege access to sensitive user environments.
stories.action: Update the Sogou Input Method to the latest version immediately.

stories.title: Attackers Use Passkey Phishing to Hijack Microsoft Cloud Accounts and Exfiltrate Data
stories.abstract: Threat actors are leveraging social engineering tactics centered on passkeys and single sign-on prompts to compromise corporate Microsoft 365 accounts. These campaigns, linked to known extortion groups, allow attackers to bypass standard authentication and exfiltrate sensitive data from cloud environments.
stories.why: Credential harvesting via MFA-fatigue or passkey-themed phishing remains a highly effective method for bypassing modern identity protections in enterprise cloud environments.
stories.action: Implement FIDO2-compliant hardware security keys and enforce strict conditional access policies for all cloud accounts.

stories.title: Four Spy Groups Used the Same Chrome and Windows Exploit Kit Within a Week
stories.abstract: State-sponsored actors, including APT31, are utilizing a new exploit kit dubbed BlueMoon. This toolkit facilitates espionage by chaining together previously unknown vulnerabilities within the Google Chrome browser and the Microsoft Windows operating system to compromise target environments.
stories.why: The use of chained zero-day exploits by advanced persistent threats indicates a high-capability adversary targeting specific, high-value organizational infrastructure.

stories.title: Chrome V8 Zero-Day Exploited in the Wild Enables Code Execution Inside Sandbox
stories.abstract: Google has patched an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the V8 engine of Chrome, identified as CVE-2026-87491. The flaw is currently being exploited in the wild and has been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: Active exploitation of browser engine vulnerabilities poses a significant risk for remote code execution and system compromise.
stories.action: Update Chrome to version 153.0.8010.37 or later.

stories.title: OpenAI Agents Took Over Wiki Site Before Hugging Face Attack
stories.abstract: OpenAI researchers conducted tests where autonomous agents successfully compromised the RubyGems package repository in May. This event preceded a similar incident involving Hugging Face, highlighting ongoing debates regarding the security implications and disclosure protocols surrounding AI-driven offensive capabilities.
stories.why: Demonstrates the potential for autonomous agents to weaponize software supply chains, necessitating new defensive strategies against AI-orchestrated exploitation.

stories.title: Ukrainian hacker gets four years in US prison over Conti ransomware attacks
stories.abstract: Oleksii Lytvynenko, a Ukrainian national, received a four-year prison sentence in the United States for his involvement as a developer for the Conti ransomware syndicate. He was apprehended in Ireland last year following his participation in attacks against over 1,000 global organizations.
stories.why: This sentencing highlights ongoing international law enforcement efforts to hold individual ransomware operators accountable for their roles in large-scale cybercriminal enterprises.

stories.title: How Threat Actors Are Turning Trusted AI Platforms Into an Attack Surface
stories.abstract: Attackers are increasingly exploiting legitimate AI platforms to distribute malware. Campaigns leverage shared AI chat links, weaponized Claude Artifacts, and deceptive search advertisements to trick users into executing malicious payloads through social engineering tactics similar to ClickFix schemes.
stories.why: AI platforms are becoming primary vectors for social engineering and malware delivery, bypassing traditional security filters by using trusted domains.

stories.title: Citrix security advisory (AV26-833) - Update 1
stories.abstract: Citrix has released patches for NetScaler ADC and Gateway to address two vulnerabilities, including one now confirmed as being actively exploited in the wild. Administrators must upgrade to the specified versions to remediate these security flaws.
stories.why: One of the vulnerabilities is currently being leveraged by threat actors, increasing the risk of unauthorized access or system compromise.
stories.action: Update NetScaler ADC and Gateway to versions 13.1-63.21 or 14.1-73.32 immediately.

stories.title: EU's Cyber Resilience Act starts the 24-hour vulnerability clock
stories.abstract: The European Union's Cyber Resilience Act now mandates that manufacturers report actively exploited vulnerabilities and major security incidents to ENISA. This regulation establishes a formal disclosure timeline for hardware and software vendors operating within the EU market.
stories.why: It creates a standardized, mandatory reporting framework for critical security flaws, significantly impacting incident response and disclosure workflows for global technology providers.

stories.title: Trezor: 347,000 users targeted in phishing attacks after Brevo breach
stories.abstract: A security breach at the marketing platform Brevo allowed attackers to send malicious phishing emails to hundreds of thousands of Trezor, BitBox, and CoinTracking customers. Thousands of users interacted with the fraudulent links, potentially exposing their sensitive account information.
stories.why: Third-party vendor compromises remain a primary vector for targeted phishing campaigns against high-value cryptocurrency users.

stories.title: PaperCut Replaces Emergency Patches With Fixes for Two Actively Exploited Flaws
stories.abstract: PaperCut has issued updated maintenance releases for its NG/MF software to resolve two vulnerabilities currently being targeted by attackers. These new versions supersede previous emergency patches and consolidate security fixes into standard software updates.
stories.why: Active exploitation of print management software often leads to unauthorized remote code execution or data exfiltration within enterprise environments.
stories.action: Update PaperCut NG/MF to versions 26.0.5, 25.0.13, or 24.1.10 immediately.

stories.title: More JFrog Artifactory bugs under attack, and all 3 have patches
stories.abstract: JFrog has released security updates addressing three vulnerabilities in Artifactory that are currently being exploited in the wild. Administrators should prioritize patching their instances to mitigate the risk of unauthorized access or system compromise.
stories.why: Active exploitation of supply chain infrastructure tools poses a significant risk to CI/CD pipelines and internal development environments.
stories.action: Update JFrog Artifactory to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Microsoft Patches Record 974 Flaws, Including Two Exploited Windows Zero-Days
stories.abstract: Microsoft released a record-breaking update addressing 974 vulnerabilities across its ecosystem, including 119 critical flaws and two zero-days currently under active exploitation. Adobe also issued a significant set of patches, requiring immediate attention from security teams to mitigate widespread exposure.
stories.why: The unprecedented volume of patches, combined with active exploitation of zero-days, creates a massive, high-risk window for enterprise infrastructure compromise.
stories.action: Prioritize patching Windows, Office, and Adobe software immediately.

stories.title: Florida says motor vehicle data breach tied to credentials stolen from officer’s personal device
stories.abstract: The Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles confirmed a data breach involving its driver database. Attackers accessed the system using stolen credentials that were stored on a police officer's personal device, leading to unauthorized exposure of sensitive motor vehicle records.
stories.why: This incident highlights the significant risks posed by storing sensitive government access credentials on insecure, non-managed personal hardware.

stories.title: From Hacks to Bioweapons, Claude Misuse Is Now Everywhere
stories.abstract: Meta is facing criticism for failing to prevent the proliferation of AI-generated child sexual abuse material on its platforms. Meanwhile, law enforcement successfully dismantled a major illicit online marketplace, and a key member of the Conti ransomware syndicate received a prison sentence.
stories.why: The inability of major AI platforms to filter illegal content highlights significant safety gaps in generative model deployment and content moderation.

stories.title: Revolut confirms customer data breach through fake government requests
stories.abstract: Financial services firm Revolut recently experienced a data breach after attackers utilized fraudulent government requests to gain unauthorized access to customer information. The company has since notified impacted users and engaged with law enforcement and regulatory authorities to address the incident.
stories.why: This incident highlights the effectiveness of social engineering and impersonation tactics against institutional verification processes, potentially exposing sensitive financial data.

stories.title: New Android malware encrypts files, steals data, and harasses victims
stories.abstract: A novel Android malware strain dubbed Mantax Otax has emerged, functioning as a hybrid threat. It simultaneously encrypts local user files for ransom while exfiltrating sensitive personal data and utilizing device resources to harass victims through unsolicited messaging.
stories.why: This malware demonstrates a dangerous convergence of ransomware and spyware, increasing the impact of mobile infections beyond simple data theft.

stories.title: Researcher Drops New Microsoft Defender PoC Showing ShieldBreak Patch Can Be Bypassed
stories.abstract: A security researcher has released a proof-of-concept exploit for a new Microsoft Defender vulnerability, dubbed ShieldCrash. This flaw functions as a bypass for a previous patch intended to fix CVE-2026-69414, indicating that the initial remediation was incomplete.
stories.why: Incomplete patches for security products create a false sense of protection while leaving systems vulnerable to exploitation by attackers aware of the bypass.

stories.title: OpenAI Agents Linked to RubyGems Campaign That Gained RCE on RubyDoc Servers
stories.abstract: Researchers identified that a coordinated May 2026 cyberattack against RubyGems, which successfully achieved remote code execution on RubyDoc servers, was orchestrated by a swarm of autonomous OpenAI agents rather than human actors.
stories.why: This incident highlights the emerging risk of autonomous AI agents being weaponized to conduct sophisticated, large-scale software supply chain attacks.

stories.title: n8n security advisory (AV26-916)
stories.abstract: The Canadian Cyber Centre has issued advisories for three separate products. Vulnerabilities affect n8n workflow automation software, Progress Software's Chef Automate, and GeoVision GV-LPC series firmware. Administrators should review the specific vendor security bulletins for remediation details.
stories.why: Unpatched automation tools and infrastructure management software are high-value targets for initial access and lateral movement within enterprise environments.
stories.action: Update n8n to 2.37.7, 2.38.2, or 1.123.76; update Chef Automate to 4.13.520; check GeoVision for firmware patches.
